sentences.text: There is delay of 1312 days in filing the appeal and I.A.No.1/2025 is filed to condone the delay.
2. Learned Government Advocate would oppose the application on the premise that sufficient cause is not shown to allow the application and to condone the delay of 1312 days.
3. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants and the learned Government Advocate.

4. This miscellaneous second appeal arises from the judgment and decree in L.A.C (Appeal)
No.363/2016 dated 20.09.2019 passed by the Principal District Judge, Hassan (for brevity, 'the Appellate Court'), wherein the award in L.A.C No.03/2006 dated 13.03.2006 passed by the Civil Judge (Senior Division) Holenarasipura (for brevity, 'the Reference Court') was under challenge by the landloser.
It is noticed that there is delay of 1312 days in filing the appeal.

5. It is submitted that the appellants are the landlosers and they have not received adequate compensation consequent to the land acquisition and they did not have the financial resource to file appeal by paying the Court fee.
NC: 2026:KHC:6813 HC-KAR 6.

It is further submitted that the appellants are the rustic villagers and they are not too familiar with the legal procedures.
7.

Considering the fact that the case is about just compensation where the landlosers are alleging that adequate compensation is not paid and also considering the fact that the beneficiary has not been made a party to the proceedings, the Court is of the view that the matter requires reconsideration after making beneficiary as a party to the proceedings.
8. Under these circumstances, I.A.No.1/2025 is allowed.
Delay of 1312 days in filing the appeal is condoned.
9. However, it is made clear that in case the compensation is enhanced, the appellants are not entitled to interest for the delayed period of 1312 days.
10. It is noticed that before the Reference Court and before the Appellate Court, the beneficiary has not been made a party in a petition seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: The settled position of law is the beneficiary should be made a party.
The Reference Court should have brought it NC: 2026:KHC:6813 HC-KAR to the notice of the claimants before adjudicating the case on merits.
12. Under these circumstances, the impugned judgment and award and impugned judgment and decree are set aside.
13. The matter is remitted to the Reference Court with a direction to the appellants/petitioners to implead beneficiary as a party to the proceedings.

14. The Reference Court shall hear the petitioners and the respondents including the beneficiary and permit them to lead evidence and thereafter, to pass award in accordance with law.
15.
In case the compensation is enhanced, the appellants will not be entitled to interest on the enhanced compensation for 1312 days.
It is made clear that this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merits of the matter.
All the contentions are kept open.
The appeal is accordingly allowed-in-part.

SD/-
(ANANT RAMANATH HEGDE)
